idiom_name: pact-cplusplus consumer DSL over libpact_ffi (Conan + CMake)
implementation_notes: pact-cplusplus provides the consumer DSL as a shared library (pact-cpp-consumer) that wraps the Rust pact_ffi core, so the classic structure is not re-implemented: pact_consumer::Pact names the consumer and provider, the given/uponReceiving/withRequest/willRespondWith chain declares one interaction, JSON bodies are assembled from matchers (Object, Integer, Like, Matching, EachLike, AtLeastOneLike, DateTime) and the run_test helper starts the mock server, runs your closure and validates the recorded interactions afterwards. Where the Conan/CMake dependency cannot be taken, the fallback is the manual route: emit the same Pact JSON from your own fixtures and replay it with the pact_verifier CLI.
pitfalls: Matchers cascade: Like/EachLike applies to everything below the node, so wrap values that must not change in EqualTo or the contract stops pinning them.
The consumer library must be linked together with pact_ffi (and, on Linux, with pthread, dl and m); a mismatched Conan package version surfaces as unresolved symbols rather than as a clear error.
Verification runs in a separate process (the pact_verifier CLI or the equivalent FFI entry point), so a provider that exists only as an in-process test fixture is unreachable and cannot be verified.
